messages.text:
Luma — heh. That's actually a good sign. 😂

For QS 1.0, the new stuff worth testing first is the archive/version protection, not the relay itself. The relay was carried forward from the working MMRC code.

Test 1 — First-launch behavior

Since you put qs.py in:

C:\Users\mcozm\projects\drsgem\QuackSink

run it normally.

You should see something along the lines of:

No matching QS archive found.

Then QS should create its first archive under that QuackSink directory, with the old date-style naming preserved plus the version number.

Test 2 — Look inside the new archive

You should find:

qs.py

qs_config.json (if the config exists)

LOG.txt

And the archive directory name should identify QS 1.0.

Test 3 — Restart QS

Close QS and launch it again.

This time QS should find its existing QS 1.0 archive and compare the running qs.py against the archived qs.py.

They should match, and QS should start normally.

Test 4 — The fun one 😈

Make a tiny change to the running qs.py—even something harmless like a comment—and launch it.

QS should detect:

internal QS 1.0 ≠ archived QS 1.0

and ERROR rather than silently accepting the mismatch.

That's the important new safety mechanism.

Test 5 — Later, when you upload an archive

Once you put the archive into your GitHub ARCHIVES 8-30-2026 structure, we can test the other half:

local QS version → archive version → source comparison → newer archive discovery/reporting.

That's the part I would test after we know the local protection works.

And one correction to my previous answer: the exact archive filename format is something I want to verify against the actual qs.py I generated rather than make you trust my memory. We have the file right here, so I can inspect it before you start changing anything.

Yep. You caught an actual omission.

The archive naming is exactly what we wanted:

QS_Aug 31 2026 12_23_55_AM_v1.0

and the archive contains the running qs.py. 👍

But the Fan-Out viewport reset is not in this QS 1.0 code. I checked the actual file: log_box.see(tk.END) is still what log() uses, and start_relay() never sends the display back to "1.0".

So don't test anything else yet. One bug at a time.

The fix belongs immediately when Fan-Out starts:

Python
Run
self.ui.clear_input()
self.ui.clear_log()
self.ui.log_box.see("1.0")

That makes the display jump to the top after the old display is cleared and before the new relay output starts, without touching the FIFO or message ordering.

And yes—your existing archive proves something important: QS 1.0 created the archive correctly on first launch. The archive machinery is doing its job.
